main_body: A narrow hospital bed seen from the head end: a grey headboard panel with dark slats on top (rows 10-21), then a white pillow and blanket with a blue stripe (rows 22-42), and a grey footboard rail at the bottom (rows 43-46).
top_band: none. The column reads: dark outline (row 10), a grey headboard face (rows 11-20), a dark beam (rows 20-21), then a white mattress/blanket face (rows 22-42). There is no horizontal surface band set apart from the front face by a step. The pillow and blanket are painted face-on, as if seen from the front or from above, with no foreshortened top and no front face below it.
evidence: The bed is drawn as a vertical stack of flat panels: headboard, pillow, blanket and footboard. The white region (rows 22-42) is a single bedding surface with no step between a top and a front face. It reads as a bed seen as a flat plank from above, or a face-on elevation, and does not show the foreshortened top plus south face required by the 3/4 contract. Fails as front elevation / top-down plan.

style.evidence: The candidate has 14 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 13 colours per tile against 17-20, so it is below them on both. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, which is good. Its dark edge pixels are 99% neutral, against 1% and 33% for the references, so the outline is near-black rather than the tinted dark material tone Beodeul uses. The grey and white ramps give about 5 steps with some highlight variation, but the bedding is smooth and carries little grain. Next to the references it looks thinner and more sticker-like.
